subject: math
title: Grade 7 Fractions, Decimals and Percents
seo_title: Grade 7 Fractions, Decimals and Percents Worksheets: Free Math Practice with Answer Key (BC Curriculum)
standard_text: Relationships between decimals, fractions, ratios, and percents
meta_desc: Free Grade 7 math worksheets on fractions, decimals and percents for the BC curriculum: repeating decimals like 1/3 = 0.333…, percents like 12.5% and 150%, comparing and ordering mixed forms, and word problems with test scores and win records. 100 questions with an answer key, good FSA numeracy practice.
key_big: A fraction is a division: 1/8 = 1 ÷ 8 = 0.125 = 12.5%. If a remainder comes back, the decimal repeats: 1/3 = 0.333…
key_sub: Multiply a decimal by 100 to get a percent: 0.4 = 40%, not 4%, and 1.5 = 150%. Put the repeat bar only over the digits that repeat: 1/6 = 0.1666…
body_html:
One amount, three ways

A fraction, a decimal and a percent can name the same amount. A fraction is a division: 34 means 3 ÷ 4 = 0.75. Percent means out of 100: 0.75 = 75%.

Fractions to decimals

Divide the numerator by the denominator. If the remainder becomes 0, the decimal terminates (ends). If a remainder comes back, the digits repeat for ever. That is a repeating decimal.

Write a repeating decimal with dots (0.333…) or with a bar over the digits that repeat. Put the bar only over the repeating part: 16 = 0.1666… = 0.16, and 511 = 0.4545… = 0.45.

Example

Write 720 as a decimal.

20 × 5 = 100, so multiply the top by 5 too: 720 = 35100.

Answer: 0.35

Repeating

Write 23 as a decimal.

20 ÷ 3 = 6 R 2. The remainder 2 comes back every time, so the 6s never stop.

Answer: 0.666… = 0.6

Decimals and percents

To change a decimal to a percent, multiply by 100 (move the point 2 places right). To change a percent to a decimal, divide by 100 (move the point 2 places left). A percent can have a decimal in it, like 12.5%, and it can be more than 100%.

Comparing and ordering

Change everything into decimals and write them with the same number of places. For a repeating decimal, write out enough digits to see the difference.

Example

Order 0.3, 13, 0.33 and 30.5% from least to greatest.

0.300, 13 = 0.333…, 0.330 and 30.5% = 0.305. Compare place by place.

Answer: 0.3, 30.5%, 0.33, 13

Win record

A team won 15 of its 24 games. What percent did it win?

1524 = 58 = 5 ÷ 8 = 0.625. Multiply by 100.

Answer: 62.5%

faq.q: What do Grade 7 students learn about fractions, decimals and percents in BC?
faq.a: The BC Grade 7 math curriculum covers the relationships between decimals, fractions, ratios and percents. Students change between the forms, including repeating decimals such as 1/3 = 0.333… and percents such as 12.5% and 150%, and use them to compare amounts and solve problems.

faq.q: What is a repeating decimal and how do you write it?
faq.a: A repeating decimal has digits that repeat for ever, such as 2/3 = 0.666… You can write it with dots or with a bar over only the digits that repeat, so 1/6 = 0.1666… has the bar over the 6 alone.

faq.q: How do you change a fraction to a percent?
faq.a: Divide the numerator by the denominator, then multiply by 100. For example, 3/8 = 3 ÷ 8 = 0.375, and 0.375 × 100 = 37.5%.

faq.q: Are fractions, decimals and percents on the Grade 7 FSA?
faq.a: The Grade 7 Foundation Skills Assessment (FSA) checks numeracy based on the BC curriculum, so working easily with fractions, decimals and percents is useful practice for it.

sets.title: Fractions and decimals, including repeating decimals

items.q: Write 14 as a decimal.
items.e: 14 = 25100 (multiply the top and bottom by 25) = 0.25. 0.4 uses the denominator as tenths, and 4 is 4 ÷ 1, the wrong way round.

items.q: Write 35 as a decimal.
items.e: 35 = 610 (multiply the top and bottom by 2) = 0.6. 0.35 just writes the digits 3 and 5 after the point.

items.q: Write 18 as a decimal.
items.e: 1 ÷ 8: write 1 as 1.000. 10 ÷ 8 = 1 R 2, 20 ÷ 8 = 2 R 4, 40 ÷ 8 = 5. So 18 = 0.125. 0.8 uses the denominator as the decimal, and 0.12 stops before the remainder is 0.

items.q: Write 720 as a decimal.
items.e: 20 × 5 = 100, so multiply the top by 5 too: 720 = 35100 = 0.35. 0.7 would be 710, 0.72 just writes the digits, and 3.5 is 7 ÷ 2, which drops the 0 in 20.

items.q: Write 925 as a decimal.
items.e: 25 × 4 = 100, so 925 = 36100 = 0.36. 0.09 forgets to multiply the top by 4, and 0.34 adds 9 + 25.

items.q: Write 0.45 as a fraction in simplest form.
items.e: 0.45 = 45 hundredths = 45100. Divide the top and bottom by 5: 920. 4510 would be 4.5.

items.q: Write 0.125 as a fraction in simplest form.
items.e: 0.125 has three decimal places, so it is 1251000. Divide the top and bottom by 125: 18. 125100 would be 1.25.

items.q: Write 13 as a decimal.
items.e: 1 ÷ 3 = 0.333… The remainder is always 1, so the 3s never stop. It is written 0.333… or 0.3 (a bar over the digit that repeats). 0.33 stops too early, so it is a little less than 13.

items.q: Write 23 as a decimal.
items.e: 2 ÷ 3: 20 ÷ 3 = 6 R 2, and the remainder 2 comes back every time. So 23 = 0.666… = 0.6. 1.5 is 3 ÷ 2, the wrong way round.

items.q: Write 49 as a decimal.
items.e: 40 ÷ 9 = 4 R 4, and the remainder 4 comes back every time. So 49 = 0.444… = 0.4. 2.25 is 9 ÷ 4, the wrong way round.

items.q: Which fraction is a repeating decimal?
items.e: 29 = 2 ÷ 9 = 0.222… The 2s never stop. The others end: 38 = 0.375, 720 = 0.35 and 45 = 0.8. In simplest form, a fraction ends as a decimal only when the denominator has no prime factors except 2 and 5.

items.q: Which fraction is a terminating decimal (it ends)?
items.e: 16 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2, so 316 ends: 3 ÷ 16 = 0.1875. 13, 56 and 47 have a factor of 3 or 7 in the denominator, so they repeat.

items.q: In the repeating decimal 0.43, which digits repeat?
items.e: The bar is only over the 3, so 0.43 = 0.4333…, and the 4 is written once. 0.43 would be 0.434343…

items.q: The division shows 1 ÷ 6. The remainder keeps coming back. What is 16 as a decimal?
items.e: 10 ÷ 6 = 1 R 4, then 40 ÷ 6 = 6 R 4, and the remainder 4 keeps coming back. Only the 6 repeats: 16 = 0.1666… = 0.16. 0.161616… repeats the 1 as well, but the 1 appears only once.

items.q: Write 712 as a decimal.
items.e: 70 ÷ 12 = 5 R 10, 100 ÷ 12 = 8 R 4, 40 ÷ 12 = 3 R 4, and the remainder 4 keeps coming back. So 712 = 0.58333… = 0.583. Only the 3 repeats. 0.583 stops too early.

items.q: The division shows 5 ÷ 11. What is 511 as a decimal?
items.e: 50 ÷ 11 = 4 R 6, 60 ÷ 11 = 5 R 5, then 50 ÷ 11 again. The two digits 4 and 5 repeat: 511 = 0.454545… = 0.45. 0.4545 stops, and 2.2 is 11 ÷ 5.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 0.1?
items.e: 1 ÷ 9 = 0.111… = 0.1, so the answer is 19. 110 is 0.1, which stops, and 111 = 0.090909…

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 0.6?
items.e: 2 ÷ 3 = 0.666… = 0.6, so the answer is 23. 610 = 0.6 ends after one 6. 16 = 0.1666…

items.q: Write 3 56 as a decimal.
items.e: The 3 wholes stay. 56 = 5 ÷ 6 = 0.8333…, so 3 56 = 3.8333… = 3.83. 0.8333… forgets the 3 wholes.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 0.45? Divide to check.
items.e: 5 ÷ 11 = 0.454545… = 0.45, so the answer is 511. 920 = 0.45 stops, and 49 = 0.444…

sets.title: Decimals and percents, including 12.5% and over 100%

items.q: Write 0.4 as a percent.
Write 0.07 as a percent.
Write 36% as a decimal.
items.e: Divide by 100: 36 ÷ 100 = 0.36. Move the decimal point 2 places to the left.

items.q: Write 5% as a decimal.
items.e: 5% = 5 hundredths. Hundredths are the second place after the point: 0.05. 0.5 is 50%.

items.q: Which shows the shaded part as a decimal and a percent?
items.e: 8 of 100 squares = 8 hundredths = 0.08 = 8%. 0.8 would be 80 squares.

items.q: Write 1 as a percent.
Write 1.5 as a percent.
items.e: 1.5 × 100 = 150, so 1.5 = 150%. More than 1 whole is more than 100%. 105% would be 1.05.

items.q: Write 2.3 as a percent.
Write 140% as a decimal.
items.e: 140 ÷ 100 = 1.4. 140% is more than 100%, so the decimal must be more than 1. 0.14 is only 14%.

items.q: Write 250% as a decimal.
items.e: 250 ÷ 100 = 2.5. 250% is 2 wholes and a half. 0.25 is only 25%.

items.q: Write 0.125 as a percent.
items.e: 0.125 × 100 = 12.5, so 0.125 = 12.5%. A percent can have a decimal in it. 125% would be 1.25.

items.q: Write 12.5% as a decimal.
items.e: 12.5 ÷ 100 = 0.125. 1.25 moves the point only one place, and 1.25 is 125%.

items.q: Write 0.875 as a percent.
items.e: 0.875 × 100 = 87.5, so 0.875 = 87.5%. Move the decimal point 2 places to the right.

items.q: Write 0.035 as a percent.
Write 0.5% as a decimal.
Each hundred grid is one whole. What percent is shaded?
items.e: One whole grid is 100%, and 35 squares of the next grid is 35%. 100% + 35% = 135% = 1.35. 35% forgets the full grid, and 65% counts the white squares.

items.q: Which decimal is more than 100%?
Which is not equal to 1.2?
items.e: 1.2 = 1.20 = 120% = 65. 12% is 0.12, only one tenth as much.

items.q: Write 3.75 as a percent.
items.e: 3.75 × 100 = 375, so 3.75 = 375%. 37.5% moves the point only one place.

items.q: Write 0.3 as a percent.
items.e: 0.3 = 0.333… Multiply by 100: 33.3…%, also written 3313%. The 3s after the point keep going.

items.q: Write 14 as a percent.
items.e: 14 = 25100 = 25%. 14% just writes the digits, and 40% uses the denominator as tenths.

items.q: Write 35 as a percent.
items.e: 35 = 60100 = 60%. 35% just writes the digits 3 and 5.

items.q: Write 710 as a percent.
items.e: 710 = 70100 = 70%. 7% would be 7100, and 30% is the part that is left.

items.q: Write 920 as a percent.
items.e: 20 × 5 = 100, so 920 = 45100 = 45%. 55% is the other part, 1120.

items.q: Write 40% as a fraction in simplest form.
items.e: 40% = 40100. Divide the top and bottom by 20: 25. 4100 is 4%, not 40%.

items.q: Write 15% as a fraction in simplest form.
items.e: 15% = 15100. Divide the top and bottom by 5: 320. 32 would be 150%.

items.q: Write 18 as a percent.
items.e: 18 = 1 ÷ 8 = 0.125 = 12.5%. 80% comes from the mistake 18 = 0.8.

items.q: Write 58 as a percent.
items.e: 58 = 5 ÷ 8 = 0.625. Multiply by 100: 62.5%. 58% just writes the digits, and 6.25% moves the point only one place.

items.q: What percent of the bar is shaded?
items.e: 3 of 8 equal parts are shaded: 38 = 3 ÷ 8 = 0.375 = 37.5%. 62.5% is the white part.

items.q: Write 12.5% as a fraction in simplest form.
items.e: 12.5% = 0.125 = 1251000. Divide the top and bottom by 125: 18. 125100 is 125%.

items.q: Write 13 as a percent.
items.e: 13 = 1 ÷ 3 = 0.333… Multiply by 100: 33.3…%, also written 3313%. 30% would be 310.

items.q: Write 23 as a percent.
items.e: 23 = 2 ÷ 3 = 0.666… Multiply by 100: 66.6…%, also written 6623%. 66% stops too early, and 150% is 32.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 33 13%?
items.e: 33 13% = 33.3…% = 0.333… = 13. 310 is 30%, and 3310 is 330%.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 85%?
items.e: 85% = 85100. Divide the top and bottom by 5: 1720. 320 is 15%, the part that is left.

items.q: Write 54 as a percent.
items.e: 54 = 5 ÷ 4 = 1.25 = 125%. The fraction is more than 1, so the percent is more than 100%. 80% is 45.

items.q: Write 1 35 as a percent.
items.e: 1 whole = 100% and 35 = 60%. 100% + 60% = 160%. 60% forgets the whole, and 135% just writes the digits.

items.q: Write 175% as a fraction in simplest form.
items.e: 175% = 100% + 75% = 1 + 34 = 1 34. 34 forgets the whole, and 1 710 is 170%.

items.q: The line from 0% to 200% is split into 8 equal parts. What percent is at the red dot?
items.e: 100% is 4 parts, so each part is 25%. The dot is 5 parts along: 5 × 25% = 125% = 1 14. 62.5% treats the whole line as 100%.

items.q: Write 0.5% as a fraction in simplest form.
items.e: 0.5% = 0.5100. Multiply the top and bottom by 2 to get rid of the decimal: 1200. 12 is 50%, not 0.5%.

items.q: Which is not equal to 75%?
items.e: 75% = 75100 = 34 = 0.75. 75 just writes the digits 7 and 5; it is 140%.

sets.title: Compare and order fractions, decimals and percents

items.q: Compare 0.4 and 4%.
Compare 18 and 0.8.
items.e: 18 = 1 ÷ 8 = 0.125. 0.125 < 0.800, so 18 < 0.8.

items.q: Compare 35 and 0.35.
items.e: 35 = 610 = 0.6 = 0.60. 0.60 > 0.35, so 35 > 0.35.

items.q: Compare 12.5% and 18.
items.e: 12.5% = 0.125, and 18 = 1 ÷ 8 = 0.125. So 12.5% = 18.

items.q: Compare 150% and 1.05.
Compare 0.3 and 0.33.
items.e: 0.3 = 0.333… and 0.33 = 0.330. The third place is 3 > 0, so 0.3 > 0.33.

items.q: Compare 23 and 0.67.
items.e: 23 = 2 ÷ 3 = 0.666… and 0.67 = 0.670. Compare the hundredths: 6 < 7. So 23 < 0.67.

items.q: Compare 56 and 0.83.
items.e: 56 = 5 ÷ 6 = 0.8333… and 0.83 = 0.830. The third place is 3 > 0, so 56 > 0.83.

items.q: Compare 37 and 0.43.
items.e: 37 = 3 ÷ 7 = 0.4285… and 0.43 = 0.4300. Compare the hundredths: 2 < 3. So 37 < 0.43.

items.q: Which is the greatest?
items.e: As decimals: 0.8 = 0.888…, 78 = 0.875, 0.850, 86% = 0.860. The greatest is 0.8.

items.q: Which is the least?
items.e: As decimals: 112 = 1 ÷ 12 = 0.0833…, 0.090, 8.5% = 0.085, 0.100. The least is 112.

items.q: Which number is between 0.4 and 0.5?
items.e: 49 = 4 ÷ 9 = 0.444…, which is between 0.4 and 0.5. 0.04 is far less, 38 = 0.375 and 51% = 0.51.

items.q:
Order from least to greatest:
0.3, 13, 0.33, 30.5%
items.e: As decimals with 3 places: 0.300, 13 = 0.333…, 0.330, 30.5% = 0.305. So 0.3, 30.5%, 0.33, 13.

items.q: Which list is in order from least to greatest?
c: 25, 49, 0.45, 46%
25, 0.45, 49, 46%
49, 25, 0.45, 46%
46%, 0.45, 49, 25
items.e: As decimals: 25 = 0.400, 49 = 0.444…, 0.450, 46% = 0.460. So 25, 49, 0.45, 46%.

items.q:
Order from greatest to least:
1.2, 115%, 1 14, 1.02
items.e: As decimals: 1.20, 115% = 1.15, 1 14 = 1.25, 1.02. Greatest first: 1 14, 1.2, 115%, 1.02.

items.q:
Order from least to greatest:
58, 0.6, 62%, 0.6
items.e: As decimals: 58 = 0.625, 0.600, 62% = 0.620, 0.6 = 0.666… So 0.6, 62%, 58, 0.6.

items.q: The line from 0 to 1 is split into 6 equal parts. What decimal is at the red dot?
items.e: Each part is 16. The dot is 5 parts along: 56 = 5 ÷ 6 = 0.8333… = 0.83. 0.5 counts the parts as tenths, and 0.83 is close but stops; the 3s keep going.

items.q: Compare 0.45 and 0.45.
items.e: Write out the digits: 0.45 = 0.4555… and 0.45 = 0.4545… The third place is 5 > 4, so 0.45 > 0.45.

items.q: Which is the greatest?
items.e: As decimals: 1.6 = 1.666…, 1.660, 1 58 = 1.625, 160.5% = 1.605. The greatest is 1.6. 1.66 stops, so it is a little less than 1.666…

items.q: Which statement is true?
items.e: 13 = 1 ÷ 3 = 0.333… = 0.3. The others are common mistakes: 0.33 stops too early, 18 = 0.125, and 0.4 = 40%.

sets.title: Word problems: test scores and win records

items.q: Ryan scores 42 out of 50 on a science test. What percent does he score?
items.e: 4250 = 84100 (multiply the top and bottom by 2) = 84%. 16% is the part he got wrong.

items.q: In a Grade 7 class of 30 students, 12 take the bus to school. What percent take the bus?
items.e: 1230 = 410 (divide by 3) = 40%. 60% is the students who do not take the bus, and 2.5% comes from 30 ÷ 12.

items.q: One November, it rained on 18 of the 30 days in Vancouver. On what percent of the days did it rain?
items.e: 1830 = 610 (divide by 3) = 60%. 40% is the days with no rain.

items.q: A Surrey soccer team has 9 wins and 3 losses, with no ties. What percent of its games did it win?
items.e: It played 9 + 3 = 12 games. 912 = 34 = 75%. 300% divides 9 by 3, the losses, instead of by all 12 games.

items.q: Noah gets 7 out of 8 questions right on a quiz. What percent is that?
items.e: 78 = 7 ÷ 8 = 0.875 = 87.5%. 12.5% is the part he got wrong, and 78% just writes the digits.

items.q: On a math test, Sofia scores 17 out of 20. Zara gets 0.84 of the marks on the same test. Who has the higher score?
items.e: 1720 = 85100 = 85% = 0.85. 0.85 > 0.84, so Sofia has the higher score.

items.q: A school raised 1.25 times as much in this year’s Terry Fox Run as last year. What percent of last year’s amount is that?
items.e: 1.25 × 100 = 125, so it is 125% of last year’s amount. More than last year means more than 100%. 25% is only the extra part.

items.q: A bike shop in Victoria sells a bike for 140% of what the shop paid for it. Write 140% as a decimal.
items.e: 140 ÷ 100 = 1.4. The shop sells the bike for 1.4 times what it paid. 0.14 is only 14%.

items.q: A Kamloops lacrosse team won 15 of its 24 games. What percent of its games did it win?
items.e: 1524 = 58 (divide by 3) = 5 ÷ 8 = 0.625 = 62.5%. 37.5% is the games it did not win, and 160% is 24 ÷ 15, the wrong way round.

items.q: Emma gets 1 of the 8 questions wrong on a quiz. What percent of the questions does she get wrong?
items.e: 18 = 1 ÷ 8 = 0.125 = 12.5%. 87.5% is the part she got right.

items.q: Chloe pours 2 L of water equally into 3 bottles for a hike near Whistler. How much water is in each bottle?
items.e: 2 ÷ 3 = 23 L = 0.666… L = 0.6 L, a little less than 0.7 L. 1.5 L is 3 ÷ 2, the wrong way round.

items.q: A quiz has 30 questions. Kai gets 0.6 of them right. How many questions does he get right?
items.e: 0.6 = 23. 23 of 30 = 30 ÷ 3 × 2 = 20. 18 uses 0.6 instead of 0.666…, and 10 is the number he gets wrong.

items.q: On a snowy day, 56 of the runs at a ski hill on Grouse Mountain are open. What decimal is that?
items.e: 5 ÷ 6: 50 ÷ 6 = 8 R 2, then 20 ÷ 6 = 3 R 2 again and again. So 56 = 0.8333… = 0.83. 1.2 is 6 ÷ 5, the wrong way round.

items.q: On a reading test, Hana gets 0.82 of the marks, Harjot gets 45 and Nadia gets 83%. Order them from highest to lowest score.
items.e: As decimals: 0.82, 45 = 0.80, 83% = 0.83. Highest first: Nadia, Hana, Harjot.

items.q: Three soccer teams compare win records. The Kelowna team won 58 of its games, the Nanaimo team won 0.6, and the Burnaby team won 61%. Which team has the best record?
items.e: As decimals: 58 = 0.625, 0.600 and 61% = 0.610. 0.625 is the greatest, so Kelowna has the best record.

items.q: Wei scores 23 of the marks on a test. Lucas scores 67%. Who has the higher score?
items.e: 23 = 0.666… = 66.6…%, and 67% = 0.67. 0.670 > 0.666…, so Lucas has the higher score, but only just.

items.q: A hockey team in Prince George won 23 of its games. Win records are often written as a decimal to 3 places. What is its win record?
items.e: 23 = 2 ÷ 3 = 0.6666… The 4th place is 6, so round up: 0.667. 0.666 cuts the digits off without rounding.

items.q: A lacrosse team won 60% of its 25 games. How many games did it win?
items.e: 60% = 35. 35 of 25 = 25 ÷ 5 × 3 = 15 games. 10 is the games it did not win, and 35 is 60 − 25.

items.q: A class collects 150% of its goal of 200 cans for the food bank. How many cans does it collect?
items.e: 150% = 1.5. 1.5 × 200 = 300 cans. 350 adds 150 + 200, and 150 is only the percent.

items.q: After 12 games, a hockey team has 7 wins, 3 losses and 2 ties. What percent of its games did it lose?
items.e: 312 = 14 = 25%. 30% uses 7 + 3 = 10 games instead of all 12, and 75% is the games it did not lose.
